safety_verdicts.content: Patient has never used an epipen in the past.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not state that the patient has never used an epipen.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the patient has previously been prescribed or used an epinephrine auto-injector helps risk-stratify for anaphylaxis and guides emergency planning and documentation. Omitting this can lead to an inaccurate allergy history and potentially suboptimal future triage if similar symptoms recur.

safety_verdicts.content: There is no evidence of cellulitis.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly state there is no evidence of cellulitis (it only advises monitoring for infection).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not explicitly stating “no evidence of cellulitis” is unlikely to cause harm when the plan already includes monitoring for spreading redness, warmth, or infection signs. This omission mainly reduces clarity of the assessment rather than changing management.

safety_verdicts.content: No allergy testing needed for this one-off episode.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention that allergy testing is not needed for a one-off episode.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document that allergy testing is not indicated after a single, localized insect sting reaction could lead to unnecessary follow-up or referral, but it does not typically pose direct clinical danger. The impact is primarily over-investigation and inefficiency.
